Neugebauer, the co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., has issued a statement in response to the company's decision to drop its lawsuit against him, which was filed to validate a 70% supermajority bylaw amendment. The lawsuit's dismissal comes after a Texas Business Court ordered Fermi to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw amendment, and Neugebauer claims that the company's actions confirm that the bylaw move was about entrenching the board's power rather than good governance. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players.

The toothbrush, called CameraJet, is the first with an integrated camera to narrow in on the gaps in the teeth and direct a precision jet at them. Bloomberg's Sam Kelly joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Ternus Takes Apple Helm Ahead of Foldable iPhone Debut
general.summary: John Ternus begins his first day as Apple CEO as the company prepares for one of its biggest product launches in years. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman explains how the longtime hardware chief will manage Apple’s veteran leadership team and what to expect from the company’s first foldable iPhone, including a price tag above $2,000. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: A Data Center Backlash - The New York Times
Can the US AI Boom Survive Data Center Backlash?
general.summary: Data centers are emerging as an issue in political races across the US as voters raise concerns about power costs and the rapid AI infrastructure buildout. Information Technology Industry Council CEO Jason Oxman discusses the tech industry’s response, growing calls to restrict new projects, and why continued investment is critical to competing with China in AI. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Finland Narrows Deficit in 2027 Budget as Economy Recovers
general.summary: Finland’s government agreed on a budget for next year that supports economic recovery while Prime Minister Petteri Orpo’s four-party coalition tries to rein in public debt growth.

general.title: Why Government Bond Yields Are Rising and Causing Alarm
general.summary: Government borrowing costs have been surging around the world as investors demand more compensation to entice them to hold longer-maturity debt. Yields on 30-year Japanese government bonds are near all-time highs at 4.19%, while 30-year UK government bond yields are at their highest since 1998. A Bloomberg gauge tracking government debt across the Group of Seven countries now yields its highest on average since September 2000.

general.title: Anthropic Says New Fable AI Model Is Cheaper, Better at Coding - Bloomberg.com
Anthropic Says New Fable 5.1 AI Model Is Cheaper, Better at Coding
general.summary: Anthropic PBC is releasing a new version of its powerful Fable artificial intelligence model that it says is better at coding and science tasks, as well as more economical — all changes it says are in response to customer feedback.

general.title: Nestle Sells Vitamins Business to PE Buyer for $1 Billion
general.summary: Nestle SA plans to sell its mainstream vitamins and supplements business to US private equity firm Yellow Wood Partners for $1 billion as Chief Executive Officer Philipp Navratil tries to streamline and turn around the Swiss foodmaker.

general.title: Apple Ternus Touts Product Pipeline, ‘Phenomenal’ Sept. 9 iPhone Launch in Memo
general.summary: Apple Inc. Chief Executive Officer John Ternus touted the company’s strong product pipeline and teased a “phenomenal” iPhone launch next week in his first remarks to employees as their new leader.

general.title: JPMorgan's Aliaga Is Upbeat on Demand for Big-Tech Debt
general.summary: Big Tech is increasingly turning to debt to finance the massive buildout of AI infrastructure. JPMorgan Asset Management's global market strategist Stephanie Aliaga explains why hyperscaler bond issuance is poised to keep growing, how the market is absorbing the new supply, and why stronger visibility into AI returns could help sustain the spending boom. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: ‘Not perfectly aligned’ with human values: Anthropic admits security failures behind AI hacking incidents - The Guardian
US Strikes Targets in Iran Around Strait of Hormuz
general.summary: The US launched strikes against Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz, following Iran's attacks on commercial shipping and American forces in the region. Oil prices are spiking on the news. Tyler Kendall reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Bessent Suggests Backing for BOJ Action in Meeting With Ueda
general.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who’s repeatedly signaled that Japan needs higher interest rates to bolster the yen, suggested he’s supporting such a move after a meeting with Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda.

general.summary: Bill Gates, the billionaire co-founder of Microsoft Corp., published a 6,000-word essay on Aug. 26 saying that he would slow the development of artificial intelligence if he could. He elaborated in an interview with the New York Times, saying “in private, people who understand how good this stuff is, and how much better it’s getting, they’re very worried” but few are raising the issues in public. general.title: Fortress’s Burton Says Rates Still Poised to Go Higher
general.summary: Global bonds slumped as rising oil prices fueled inflation fears and bets on Fed rate hikes. Fortress Chief Strategist Elizabeth Burton says rates are still poised to go higher, arguing the underlying problem won’t be fixed without a fiscal response. She speaks on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Crypto enters September with legislative policy gamble hanging by a thread
general.summary: Comprehensive industry legislation teeters on the brink amid growing doubts the bill will cross the finish line.

general.title: Apple enters John Ternus era as AI challenges and memory crunch intensify
general.summary: John Ternus' first day as Apple CEO comes at a critical juncture for the iPhone maker, with memory prices soaring and AI challenges looming.

general.title: AI costs drop while demand surges - CNBC
Oil Prices Spike as US Retaliates for Attacks by Iran
general.summary: Oil rose for a second session as fresh hostilities between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, where crude carriers were hit by projectiles. Leslie Palti-Guzman, Founder at Energy Vista, discusses the outlook for global energy as conflict in the Middle East continues to disrupt flow. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: AI for Government Relations: How Teams Turn Policy Intelligence Into Action - Bloomberg Government
Carney Says Trade Talks Can Resume If US Stops ‘Throwing Shade’
general.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said he still believes there’s a “mutually beneficial” trade deal to be done with the US, but discussions can’t resume while Trump administration officials are publicly insulting Canada.

general.title: Wells Fargo Analysts Join JPMorgan Traders in Turning Cautious on US Stocks
general.summary: Wells Fargo & Co. joins a growing chorus of voices that are cautioning on US stocks this week as the market heads into what is historically the worst month on the calendar for equities and upcoming midterm elections add to uncertainty surrounding the artificial-intelligence trade.
